quiz.title: Increasing & Decreasing Functions Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the sign of f'(x), intervals of increase and decrease, and strict monotonicity — exactly the ideas tested in Exercise 6.2. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Application of Derivatives, Exercise 6.2

questions.q: A differentiable function f is strictly increasing on an interval when, for every x in it, f'(x) is:
questions.explanation: A positive derivative means the tangent slopes upward everywhere on the interval, so the function values keep rising. f'(x) > 0 is the test for strictly increasing.

questions.q: On which interval is f(x) = x² strictly increasing?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 2x, which is positive only when x > 0. So the parabola rises on (0, ∞) and falls on (−∞, 0).

questions.q: For f(x) = x³, which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 3x² is never negative and is zero only at the single point x = 0, so f is strictly increasing on the whole of R.

questions.q: For f(x) = 2x³ − 3x² − 36x + 7, we get f'(x) = 6(x − 3)(x + 2). The function is increasing on:
questions.explanation: The product 6(x − 3)(x + 2) is positive when both factors share a sign, i.e. x < −2 or x > 3. So f increases on (−∞, −2) and (3, ∞), and decreases on (−2, 3).
f'(x) = eₓ, which is positive for every real x. So the exponential function is strictly increasing on the whole real line.

questions.q: On what interval is f(x) = x² − 4x + 6 decreasing?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 2x − 4, which is negative when x < 2. So the function decreases on (−∞, 2) and increases on (2, ∞).

questions.q: If f'(x) < 0 for every x in an interval, then on that interval f is:
questions.explanation: A negative derivative means the slope is downward throughout, so the values fall as x rises. That is the definition of strictly decreasing.

questions.q: For f(x) = log x with x > 0, the function is:
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 1/x, which is positive for all x > 0. So the logarithm is strictly increasing throughout its domain, not just beyond x = 1.

faq.q: How do you tell if a function is increasing or decreasing in Exercise 6.2?
faq.a: Differentiate the function, then check the sign of f'(x). Where f'(x) > 0 the function is increasing; where f'(x) < 0 it is decreasing. Solving f'(x) = 0 gives the boundary points that split the number line into these intervals.

faq.q: What is the difference between increasing and strictly increasing?
faq.a: A function is increasing if its values never fall as x rises (f'(x) is at least 0). It is strictly increasing if its values always rise (f'(x) > 0, allowing zeros only at isolated points). For example, x³ is strictly increasing on R even though f'(0) = 0.

faq.q: How do you find the intervals of increase and decrease?
faq.a: Set f'(x) = 0 to locate the critical points, mark them on the number line, then test the sign of f'(x) in each resulting interval. Positive intervals are increasing and negative ones are decreasing.

faq.q: Is a constant function increasing or decreasing?
faq.a: Neither. A constant function has f'(x) = 0 everywhere, so its value never rises or falls. It is treated as neither strictly increasing nor strictly decreasing.
